hints.title: Leading Bit Dominance
hints.text: The highest-order bit in each row contributes more than all subsequent bits combined.

hints.title: Row Normalization via First Column
hints.text: Ensure the leading bit of every row becomes one by flipping rows whose first value is zero.

hints.title: Independent Column Maximization
hints.text: For each subsequent column, count how many elements match their row head. Take the maximum between that count and its complement.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def matrixScore(self, grid: List[List[int]]) -> int:
        m, n = len(grid), len(grid[0])
        ans = m * (1 << (n - 1))
        for j in range(1, n):
            same_as_row0 = sum(grid[i][j] == grid[i][0] for i in range(m))
            count1 = max(same_as_row0, m - same_as_row0)
            ans += count1 * (1 << (n - 1 - j))
        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Evaluate contribution of each column independently without altering input grid.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Searching across all 2^(M+N) combinations of row and column flips causes exponential timeout.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognize that row flips must enforce 1 in the most significant bit, making column flips independent.
